## Pull request overview

This pull request adds comprehensive Storybook integration for the ObjectUI monorepo, including stories for all 14 plugin packages and reorganizing the existing component stories.

**Changes:**
- Moved Storybook configuration from package-level (`packages/components/.storybook/`) to repository root (`.storybook/`)
- Created 14 new story files for plugin components (aggrid, calendar, charts, chatbot, code-editor, dashboard, kanban, markdown, object-form, object-gantt, object-grid, object-map, object-view, timeline)
- Reorganized existing stories into a new category structure (Schema/Actions, Schema/Inputs, Schema/Layout, Schema/Data Display, Schema/Navigation, Schema/Feedback, Schema/Plugins)
- Fixed plugin component infinite loop issues in ObjectMap, ObjectGrid, and ObjectGantt by adding useMemo for dataConfig
- Refactored toggle-group component to use `selectionType` instead of `groupType`
- Added CI workflow for Storybook testing via Playwright
- Configured Vercel deployment for Storybook static build

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 70 out of 73 changed files in this pull request and generated 21 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `.storybook/main.ts` | New root-level Storybook configuration with Vite aliases for plugin packages |
| `.storybook/preview.ts` | New preview configuration importing all plugin packages and setting up story sorting |
| `packages/components/.storybook/*` | Removed old package-level Storybook configs (moved to root) |
| `packages/components/src/stories-json/*.stories.tsx` | 14 new plugin stories + reorganized 35+ existing stories into new categories |
| `packages/plugin-*/src/*.tsx` | Added useMemo pattern to prevent infinite loops in data fetching |
| `packages/components/src/renderers/disclosure/toggle-group.tsx` | Renamed `groupType` to `selectionType` and extracted type prop |
| `packages/components/src/renderers/form/toggle.tsx` | Fixed enum property naming issue (changed `index` to `enum`) |
| `packages/components/src/index.css` | Updated @source path for Tailwind scanning |
| `package.json` | Added Storybook scripts and dependencies at root level |
| `.github/workflows/storybook-tests.yml` | New CI workflow for automated Storybook testing |
| `vercel.json` | Configuration for Storybook deployment |
| `postcss.config.mjs` | Added PostCSS configuration for Tailwind |
</details>

Story data contains "Schema/Plugins/" prefix in section titles which appears to be incorrectly copy-pasted from the Storybook category path. Section titles like 'Schema/Plugins/Personal Information', 'Schema/Plugins/Contact Details' should just be 'Personal Information', 'Contact Details'.

The meta.title defines the Storybook category ('Schema/Plugins/Object Form'), but the actual data items within stories should have plain titles without the category prefix.

Story data contains "Schema/Feedback/" prefix in the title which appears to be incorrectly copy-pasted from the Storybook category path. The title should just be 'Edit profile', not 'Schema/Feedback/Edit profile'.

The meta.title defines the Storybook category ('Schema/Feedback/Dialog'), but the actual data items within stories should have plain titles without the category prefix.

According to Guideline #2 (Documentation Driven Development), any feature implemented or refactored must include corresponding documentation updates. This PR adds:
- New Storybook configuration at the repository root
- 14 new plugin story files
- Moves Storybook from package-level to monorepo-level

However, there are no documentation updates in content/docs/guide/ to explain:
- How to run Storybook (the new pnpm storybook command)
- The new Storybook structure and organization
- How to add new stories for future components

Consider adding documentation in content/docs/guide/ or updating the relevant package README files to reflect the new Storybook setup and usage patterns.

Using JSON.stringify in the dependency array of useMemo defeats its purpose and creates a performance anti-pattern. On every render, JSON.stringify creates a new string, causing the useMemo to recompute every time even if the actual data hasn't changed.

Instead, consider one of these approaches:
1. Use a deep comparison library like react-fast-compare or use-deep-compare-effect
2. List specific primitive dependencies from rawDataConfig (e.g., rawDataConfig?.provider, rawDataConfig?.object)
3. Use useRef to store the previous value and do a manual deep comparison if truly necessary

The current implementation provides no memoization benefit while adding the computational cost of JSON.stringify on every render.

Using JSON.stringify for deep comparison in setState is inefficient and creates unnecessary computational overhead on every effect run. This pattern performs serialization twice (once for prev, once for newItems) on every render when hasInlineData is true.

Consider using a dedicated deep comparison library like fast-deep-equal, or better yet, rely on React's built-in object identity checks if the data source properly memoizes the items array.

The property name should be 'enum' not 'index'. This is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase where 'enum' is used to specify the allowed values for enum type inputs (see button-group.tsx, separator.tsx, carousel.tsx, etc.).

Change 'index' to 'enum' to maintain consistency with the established pattern.
```suggestion
      { name: 'variant', type: 'enum', enum: ['default', 'outline'], defaultValue: 'default', label: 'Variant' },
      { name: 'size', type: 'enum', enum: ['default', 'sm', 'lg'], defaultValue: 'default', label: 'Size' },
```
